Hello all! A few weeks ago I ran a game called the evolution game, found here. I was a blast and it made me re-purpose an old sub of mine v/evol/. I wanted to go ahead and run another game here with the hopes of attracting new players. Eventually I will keep it all on my subverse, but until then - v/whatever/ needs to suffer my ms paint games. Here is an example of a single base species evolution tree, to show you how the game works.

The game is very simple. You start with a base creature or creatures and edit them via MS paint (or whatever program you prefer). The #1 rule is to ALWAYS SAVE AS .png. It keeps things from going all potatoey. Edit a creature in paint and upload it. If you are evolving someone else's creature, reply to their comment. If you change the name of a creature - you have created a splinter-species. If you keep it the same, you are evolving the main species (both of these points don't have very much impact on the game itself). Keep your creations believable, but don't feel too limited. You can evolve any creature you want as many times as you want, no one owns a creature.

Lastly - have some fun! This is just a creative exercise and not to be taken seriously. So, if you will allow me, I will introduce you to the creatures and their habitat.

Our beautiful organisms.

We are in a large sea. Land is not too far away and neither is the Great Ocean. For now we enjoy lots of sunshine and soft waves.

Wo - a small lilly-pad like plant. It has a long stem and reaches its main leaf as close to the surface as possible.

Crod - A shrimp-like predator. It feeds on Tads.

Tad - A small fish-like creature. It feeds on Wo.

This game will end at midnight on 8/10/2016 EST. This game will also be consistent with the current v/evol/ universe. I will update an evolution tree and include it in the OP as often as I can. Thank you all, and let's play!
The Evolution game, take 2! (new players welcome and encouraged)

The unarmored tails of Tadiro were susceptible to attack from behind. Individuals with shorter tails were selected for among future generations of Tadiro.

Larger, downward facing mouths and longer lower fins also allowed Tadiro to thrive on the sea floor.
